name: Grigori Rasputin
role: Siberian peasant mystic and faith healer at the court of Nicholas II (died 1916)
summary: Rasputin was a Siberian peasant pilgrim and healer who gained influence at court by treating the heir's haemophilia. He left no political programme; his own writings are religious reflections praising simplicity, and witnesses report that he opposed Russia's entry into the 1914 war and predicted the empire's ruin.

notes: Rules 7, later pass (first pass 2026-10-23; this pass brings the audit up to rules 7). Rasputin left no political programme, and almost every account of his politics is hostile or secondhand. Sources read: his own writing 'My Thoughts and Reflections' (1915) in a translator's excerpt with the Russian original (Lavra reflection, 1911, and 'Life of an Experienced Wanderer' excerpts on monasteries, clergy, pilgrimage), and Anna Vyrubova's memoir (Gutenberg 59564, 254 mentions of him), searched for the war, the Duma, ministers, Jews, peasants and land. The earlier war-builds-character answer (-1, Wikipedia and a reference compilation) is nulled with a reviewHistory entry: opposing the 1914 war and predicting ruin does not state whether war builds a nation's character. New answers: simple-living and consumerism-harmful (+1 medium each, his 1911 Lavra reflection; words only, as he has no recorded act on them). Themes searched with nothing that settles a statement: war and foreign policy, the Duma and ministers (Vyrubova denies he appointed ministers such as Sturmer), Jews and pogroms (no passage in Vyrubova or the excerpts), peasants, property and land, clergy and church governance (his criticism of the clergy's lack of spiritual life is a complaint, not a position on church-state relations), women and marriage. Failing the uncertainty rule is the honest result for a figure with this record.
